key_insight: Measuring example-level neuron activation patterns identifies small, high‑impact instruction examples; training on these neuron‑aware subsets improves or preserves LLM capabilities while avoiding degradation from excessive instruction data.
problem_solved: Instruction tuning with large, uncurated datasets can hurt or waste compute; the paper solves how to pick a compact, effective subset of instruction data that builds specific or general abilities without performance loss.
method: Record neuron activation signatures for candidate instruction examples using a pretrained LLM backbone (or probe neurons linked to target behaviors).
Score and rank examples by neuron‑aware criteria (e.g., activation alignment, information gain, or diversity over important neurons) to select a compact subset.
Fine‑tune the LLM on the selected subset and validate improvements on targeted tasks and general benchmarks.
impact: Enables more efficient, targeted instruction tuning—reducing compute and data while improving or maintaining model capability—useful for practitioners aiming to build specialized skills or cost‑effective generalists.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data → neuron activation extraction → scoring/ranking → selected subset → fine‑tuning → evaluation
Neuron activation heatmap showing example signatures and clusters (to illustrate selection criteria)
Line/bar chart: performance vs. fraction of training data (showing small subset outperforming or matching full dataset)
Icon grid or mosaic of selected vs. discarded instruction examples to convey dataset compression and diversity
paper_title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection In Instruction Tuning For Large Language Models
paper_authors: Xin Chen, Junchao Wu, Shu Yang, Runzhe Zhan, Zeyu Wu
